question: In ancient India, the Mahajanapada of 'Anga' had its capital at which city in Bihar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Champa**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

 
 
• **Anga** was one of the sixteen **Mahajanapadas** (great kingdoms) mentioned in ancient Indian texts such as the **Anguttara Nikaya** and the **Mahabharata**. The Mahajanapadas were the political and territorial units that flourished during the 6th century BCE. 
 
• The capital of the **Mahajanapada of Anga** was **Champa**, which was located in present-day Bihar. It was a significant city in ancient India and served as a center of trade and commerce. 
 
• **Champa** was situated on the banks of the **Ganga River** and had access to waterways, which facilitated its role as a prominent trade hub. The city was especially known for its wealth and luxury. 
 
• The kingdom of Anga played a vital role in ancient Indian history and was later annexed by the kingdom of **Magadha**, which eventually became one of the most powerful Mahajanapadas.
